name: Ocean West Boutique Hotel
brand_truth: Ten gem-named rooms in a pink colonial house on a ridge seventy feet above the sea, between Lake Killarney and the Atlantic, five minutes from the airport.
buyer: US couples and business travellers planning on a phone; compare with Cable Beach resorts and Airbnb; want the room seen, the price range clear, the airport close.

direction.why: The product is ten distinct rooms, so the room register is the hero; the hotel is literally pink stucco; a Didone reads as engraving for gem names.

big_idea: The room register is the front door: ten stones in a fixed index column; touch a name and that room appears on the stage with its bed, floor and view, and Check dates opens innRoad.
tier_why: Ten rooms are explained by their own photographs and a hover swap; 3D adds nothing.
concept_type: booking: ten-room picker with views, rates range, Check dates handing off to innRoad

revisions: fixed 4:3 stage frame (no jump on hover), aligned to the h1
register rows taller, flush, active marked by a rule; filter moved into the register
one CTA per screen (stage link only when a room is selected)
phone gem row unboxed, snapping, active underlined, Terrace first
comparison list replaced by one room in full (Emerald)

current_site_findings: Every page has the same keyword-stuffed title, so Google cannot tell the pages apart.
Headings are pictures inside tables: phones and search engines cannot read them.
Address and phone are not on the homepage.
Ten gem-named rooms appear as small thumbnails with no way to compare beds, views or balconies.
The 70 ft ridge between Lake Killarney and the Atlantic is a single sentence.
pitch_line: Your ten rooms have names most hotels would envy; this concept makes them the front door: touch Emerald and see the arched window over the sea, then book it on your own engine instead of paying the OTAs.
